title: Flow-metering harness and tenant SLA benchmark playbook
creator: Priya Mehta
description: Goal: produce a reproducible load testing harness and a runbook that programmatically verifies tenant-level throughput guarantees for Dedicated pools. Deliverables: (1) flow-metering harness (tenant-mix sampler + generator) that can emulate customer request distributions with configurable KV-cache hit patterns; (2) a benchmark methodology that produces an SLO fingerprint (p50/p95/p99 latency at target QPS) and a cost/throughput curve; (3) a customer acceptance checklist and automated signoff artifacts (dashboard snapshot + evidence bundle). This ticket focuses on the measurement methodology and on creating artifacts that external teams (Solutions, Customer Success) can use during handoffs.
acceptance_criteria: Flow-metering harness is runnable from CI with a single command and accepts a tenant-mix YAML describing request size distribution, model variant, and cache-hit target
Benchmark methodology defines a quantile-preserving ramp pattern, warmup/minimum-run-time, and statistical significance threshold
Generated benchmark report contains SLO fingerprint (p50/p95/p99), observed token/sec, cost estimate per 1M tokens, and failure modes observed
Customer acceptance checklist items are automated where possible (dash snapshot link, PR with results, audit-ready CSV) and validated in a pilot with one early customer
Artifacts and run instructions are linked in the Dedicated Capacity onboarding Confluence page and referenced in the Console release notes
steps: Design tenant-mix schema (weights, request templates, model variant mapping, KV-cache-hit target)
Implement generator: request sampler -> request emitter with pacing controller -> response validator (latency + correctness schema)
Add backend probes to collect token-level telemetry (per-route qps, avg/kvmiss latency, GPU utilization) using the existing telemetry exporter
Define ramp: 10m warmup at 10% of target QPS, linear ramp to target over 15m, sustain at target for 30m, 20m cooldown; repeat runs x3
Run against staging Dedicated pool (staging-dedicated-2) with tenant-isolation flags enabled and collect run artifacts
Produce report generator that summarizes percentiles, tail behavior, resource saturation points, and provides suggested autoscaler configurations
Run pilot with Customer X (sandbox) and collect signoff metrics and dashboard snapshots
telemetry_queries: avg(latency_ms) by quantile where model='gptx-16k' and route in ('gen','chat')
sum(tokens_generated) / sum(seconds) as tokens_per_sec by pool_id
comments: 2025-02-19 Priya Mehta: Kickoff w/ Solutions + CS. Agreed to prioritize a tenant-mix that represents 70% short-gen (<=64 tokens), 20% medium (65-1024), 10% embeddings. Decision: separate KV-cache hit targets for heavy vs light tenants.

2025-02-24 Miguel Santos (eng review): Implementation note — pacing controller should support poisson and constant-rate modes; prefer poisson for realistic burstiness. Miguel requested a tracer tag for run_id for easier log correlation.

2025-02-27 Design feedback (Sofia Martinez): Proposed benchmark report template looks dense; suggested adding an executive summary with actionable recommendations (autoscaler knobs, suggested reserved QPS).

2025-03-01 Liam O'Connor: First harness prototype ran against staging; observed two failure modes: (1) cache churn causing p95 jumps when tenant mix includes >40% medium requests; (2) occasional tail spikes linked to GC pauses in the metrics exporter. Filed follow-ups ENG-246821 and ENG-246822.

2025-03-03 Customer pilot (Customer-Beta) completed — acceptance checklist passed except for one recurring 99th percentile spike at peak. Reason appears to be contention for quantized-kernel slots; mitigation involves kernel-selection throttling and per-tenant QoS, tracked in ENG-247001.
notes: Trade-offs considered: longer sustain windows increase confidence but cost more; settled on 30m sustain for pilot runs with option to extend for enterprise audits.
We intentionally avoid synthetic all-small or all-large mixes — aim is tenant-proportional sampling to expose multi-tenant interference.
Autoscaler recommendations will include a 'safety margin' (20% headroom) and a slow scale-down policy (cooldown 10m) to avoid oscillation with bursty tenants.
